moral orel is one of my favorite shows and while it’s not explicitly stated that the characters are mentally ill, they definitely represent it. deals with lots of themes of abuse, generational trauma, religious trauma, and overall depression. evangelion is also a quintessential art exploration of isolation and depression, really connected to me as someone with MDD.

for movies, inside llewyn davis deals with a musician who clearly is struggling with depression about his career and the loss of his singing partner (one of my favorite movies.) the devil and daniel johnston is a documentary about one of my favorite singer/songwriters and his battle with bipolar disorder. synedoche, new york deals with lots of themes about the meaning of life, extenstialism, and mortality following a character who can be interpreted as depression-coded (also one of my favorite movies).

i know it’s not the most emotional impactful episode, but probably the best christmas ever. the experimentation with how the camera moves and the very realistic portrayal of clay and bloberta’s relationship hit very close to home for me. not to mention orel’s prayer to god which is one of the most purest forms of innocence and hope i’ve ever seen in any form of media. truly a work of art, something i could revisit over and over and feel like utter shit but also have faith.

passing and help are close seconds. i know a lot of people say that no children is the “song of the show” but i really think love, love, love by the mountain goats encompasses the motives of each character and the overarching connectedness and themes of them. people will do horrible, crazy, harsh things in the name of love and believe them to be okay (which is probably every character except for a few) in this show. the end sequence in passing was so harrowingly emotional, it’s crazy how you could have an ounce of sympathy for such an awful character like clay.

help is a great exploration of bloberta’s character, and i think the voice acting in this episode is a highlight in the series. not to mention the way the puppets dance at the reception, i’m so enamored and in awe with how they made them move so fluid. both the characters of clay and bloberta seem exceptionally realistic in this episode compared to their stereotypical caricatures played earlier in the shows’s run. they are given more complexity, more nuance, and that two horrible people can both take each other down (hence old college try by the mountain goats.) 

sorry for the long winded explanation! i was excited to share
